5. 1. **Atomize exploration chains.** Never combine multiple unfamiliar-path
6.    probes into one `&&` / `|` chain with `2>/dev/null` suppression — it

10. 2. **Prefer Bash heredocs over the editor `edit` AND `create` tools for large writes.**
11.    Both `edit` and `create` hang on large / many-line operations (the
12.    `create` tool stresses the IDE renderer the same way `edit` does when
13.    `file_text` is large — empirically anything > ~10 KB or > ~100 lines).
14.    For whole-file authoring use `cat > file <<'EOF' ... EOF`; for in-place
15.    transforms use `python3 - <<'PY' ... PY`. The `edit` tool is reserved
16.    for small, uniquely-anchored surgical replacements; the `create` tool
17.    is reserved for short new files (< ~10 KB / < ~100 lines). See
18.    [`ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md` §2.3.2](ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md).
19. 3. **Never nest heredocs inside heredocs.** When using
20.    `python3 - <<'PY'` whose body contains a Python triple-quoted string,
21.    the inner content MUST NOT contain heredoc-sentinel-looking tokens
22.    (`EOF`, `PY`, `MARKEREOF`, etc.) or fenced code blocks — the outer
23.    heredoc terminates early and the call silently hangs. Use a
24.    two-stage `cat > /tmp/payload <<'ZZZ_UNIQUE_ZZZ'` then a separate
25.    `cat > /tmp/script.py <<'ZZZ_OTHER_ZZZ'` then run the script. Each
26.    stage carries one heredoc with a body-unique sentinel. See
27.    [`ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md` §2.3.3](ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md).
28. 4. **Bound tool-output size AND cumulative scrollback to protect the IDE renderer.** Large outputs
29.    streamed into the chat transcript (recursive `grep -r` over many-file
30.    trees, `cat` on minified bundles, full dumps of files like
31.    `workbench.desktop.main.js`) can freeze the VS Code renderer; the user's
32.    only recovery is to force-quit, which reports every in-flight tool call
33.    back as `interrupted` and drops live shell sessions. Default behavior:
34.    redirect large commands to `/tmp/out.txt` first, then `head` / `grep` /
35.    `view` it; prefer the built-in `grep` / `glob` / `view` tools over
36.    shell-side recursive scans; narrow scope with `glob` before `grep`; and
37.    never combine "produce a large output" with "read a large file" in the
38.    same tool-call batch. See
39.    [`ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md` §2.3.4](ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md).
40.    Single-output size is necessary but not sufficient — long sessions also

43.    file-write over stdout for intermediate artifacts, do NOT re-print
44.    content already in scrollback, skip trailing verification dumps, and
45.    pause-to-consolidate after ~20 tool calls per user message. See
46.    [`ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md` §2.3.4.1](ai-agent-rules/shell-execution-rules.md).
47. 5.  **Prefer scripts over prose instructions.** Scripts are more deterministic
48.     than rules, skills, or sub-agent prompts. When designing or refactoring a

50.     (parse, transform, validate, file-mutate) MUST live in an executable

10. # Gitignore Whitelist Pattern Skill (v1)
11. 
12. > **Skill ID:** `gitignore-whitelist-pattern`
13. > **Version:** 1.0.0
14. > **Standard:** [Agent Skills (agentskills.io)](https://agentskills.io)
15. 
16. ## Description
17. 
18. Generate a **deny-all + selective whitelist** `.gitignore` block for directories that
19. must track only a narrow set of file extensions (e.g., `.7z`, `.zip`) and Git
20. configuration files (`.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`), while ignoring everything else —
21. including extracted folders, temp files, and any future additions that do not match the
22. whitelist.
23.

8. # Git .gitignore Handling Rules
9. 
10. This document defines the mandatory protocol for managing `.gitignore` files. The goal is to separate standard,
11. auto-generated exclusions (OS, IDE, Language) from project-specific custom rules using a "Generated Foundation + User
12. Delta" approach.
13. 
14. ***
15. 
16. ## 1. Source of Truth: The API
17. 
18. Whenever standardized gitignore rules are required (e.g., for Linux, macOS, Windows, VisualStudioCode), the agent
19. **MUST** source them directly from the `gitignore.io` API (via toptal.com) rather than attempting to write them
20. manually or copy-paste partial hunks.
21. 
22. - **API Endpoint**: `<https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/<list,of,templates>`>
23. 
24. - **Example**: `<https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/linux,macos,windows`>
25. 
26. - **Reference list**: `<https://docs.gitignore.io/use/api#get-all-templates`>
27. 
28. ***
29. 
30. ## 2. Workflow: Generated vs. Custom Separation
31. 
32. When processing a `.gitignore` file that contains both standard and custom rules:
33. 
34. ### Step 1: Backup and Analysis
35. 
36. 1. **Backup** the existing `.gitignore`file (if it exists) to a tailored backup location (e.g.,`.gitignore.bak`).
37. 
38. 1. **Analyze** the backup to identify:
39. 
40. - Standard categories (OS, IDE, Frameworks).
41. 
42. - User-defined customizations (specific file exclusions, un-ignore rules, or modified standard rules).
43. 
44. ### Step 2: Commit A - The Standard Foundation
45. 
46. 1. **Fetch** the standard rules using the API.
47. 
48.     ```bash
49.     curl -L -s <https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/linux,macos,windows> > .gitignore
50.     ```
51. 
52.     *(Note: Add/Remove templates as appropriate for the specific commit scope).*
53. 
54. 1. **Commit** this clean, generated file.
55. 
56. - **Title Format**: `chore(git): add <template1>, <template2> gitignore rules`
57. 
58. - **Body**: Explicitly state the source.
59. 
60.     ```text
61.     Sourced from gitignore.io (https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/...)
62.     ```
63. 
64. ### Step 3: Commit B - The User Delta
65. 
66. 1. **Compare** the current API-generated `.gitignore`with the backup (`.gitignore.bak`).
67. 
68. 1. **Identify the Delta**: Find lines present in the backup that are NOT in the API version. These are the user's
69. 
70.    custom rules.
71. 
72. 1. **Apply** these valid custom rules to the `.gitignore` file (append or patch).
73. 
74. 1. **Commit** the user-defined rules.
75. 
76. - **Strategy**:
77.       - **Single Commit**: If the delta is small or logically unified (e.g., all Supabase rules), commit as one unit.
78.       - **Multiple Commits**: If the delta contains distinct concerns (e.g., Supabase rules + unrelated private file
79.           exclusions), split them into separate atomic commits.
80. 
81. - **Title Format**: `feat(git): add project-specific gitignore rules`or`config(<scope>): add custom ignore rules`
82. 
83. - **Body**: Describe the specific custom rules being added.
84.

90. 
91.     Rules](./markdown-generation-rules.md)**.
92. 
93. - **Do not mix scopes**: If you are adding OS rules, do not slip in IDE rules in the same commit if they can be
94.

13. ## Description
14. 
15. Audit `.gitignore` files for structural errors and common pitfalls that
16. cause rules to silently fail. The most critical pattern this skill
17. detects is the **directory-ignore + negation failure**: when a directory
18. is ignored with a trailing slash (`dir/`), Git stops descending into it
19. entirely, so any negation patterns (`!dir/*.ext`) that follow are
20. **silently ignored** — the intended files are never tracked.
21. 
22. This skill scans for these and other pitfalls, applies safe fixes,
23. and verifies correctness using `git check-ignore`.
24. 
25. ## Prerequisites
26. 
27. | Requirement | Minimum |
28. |---|---|
29. | VCS | Git 2.x+ |
30. | Shell | PowerShell 5.1+ or Bash 4+ |
31. | Access | Write access to the repository |
32. 
33. ## When to Apply
34. 
35. Apply this skill when:
36. 
37. - A user asks to review, audit, or fix `.gitignore` rules
38. - A user reports that ignored files are not being tracked despite negation patterns
39. - A user adds new `.gitignore` rules with directory ignores and negations
40. - `git status` does not show files the user expects to be tracked
41. - A new `.gitignore` is being created with selective ignore/track patterns
42. 
43. Do NOT apply when:
44. 
45. - The user explicitly wants to ignore an entire directory with no exceptions
46. - The `.gitignore` contains only simple file-pattern rules (no negations)
47. - The user says "just commit it, no review needed"

51. ## Core Concept: Directory-Ignore vs Contents-Ignore
52. 
53. This is the single most important distinction in `.gitignore`:
54. 
55. | Pattern | Git Behavior | Negations Work? |
56. |---|---|---|
57. | `dir/` | Ignores the **directory itself** — Git will not descend into it | **No** — negations are silently ignored |
58. | `dir/*` | Ignores all **contents** of the directory — Git still enters it | **Yes** — negations are evaluated |
59. 
60. ### Why This Matters

300. | Nested file cannot be negated | Parent directory is fully ignored | Un-ignore each intermediate directory level |
301. | `.gitignore` change has no effect on existing file | File was previously committed and is tracked | Run `git rm --cached <file>` to untrack |
302. | Pattern fails on some systems | Trailing whitespace in `.gitignore` line | Trim trailing whitespace |
303. | `*.log` ignores too much | Overly broad glob in root `.gitignore` | Move pattern to a subdirectory `.gitignore` or use path-qualified pattern |
304. | Double-star confusion | `**/dir` vs `dir/` vs `dir/**` have different semantics | `**/dir` matches at any depth; `dir/**` matches contents at any depth inside `dir` |
305.

## Pitfall: Folder-Ignore Hides Future Schema Additions

When ignoring **ephemeral state** inside a folder whose **future schema is
unknown** (third-party tool spool dirs, IDE per-session storage, generated
caches with versioned layouts), do **NOT** ignore the parent folder. Ignore
only the *known-ephemeral leaves* so any new sibling file the tool starts
emitting later surfaces as untracked in `git status` for explicit review.

### Wrong (over-broad — silent future drift)

```gitignore
# Hides everything the tool may emit later, including
# files the user would actually want to version-control.
some/tool/per-session/*/
```

### Right (narrow leaves — unknown siblings surface)

```gitignore
# Ignore only the leaves we have audited as ephemeral.
# Anything new the tool emits in this folder later will
# show up as untracked and force a deliberate decision.
some/tool/per-session/*/state.json
some/tool/per-session/*/contents/
```

### Canonical Real-World Case: VS Code Copilot Chat `chatEditingSessions`

`workspaceStorage/<workspace-hash>/chatEditingSessions/<sessionId>/` contains:

| Path | Status | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `state.json` | **Ignore** | Per-chat-turn undo/redo timeline; rewritten on every turn; canonical edit history already lives in the repo's commit log. |
| `contents/` | **Ignore** | Content-addressed snapshots of pre/post-edit file text; pure redundant churn vs Git's own blob store. |
| (future sibling files) | **Do not pre-ignore** | VS Code may add new per-session artifacts later; let them surface for triage. |

### Companion `.gitattributes` Cleanup

When narrowing an ignore rule, also audit `.gitattributes` for any
`filter=` / `diff=` / textconv lines that targeted the now-ignored leaves —
they become dead config. Example: removing the `state.json` `jq-pretty`
filter line once `state.json` is ignored.

### Audit Cue

When asked to ignore "this whole VS Code / IDE / tool state folder", first
ask: **"What are all the leaf files actually in there, and is the schema
stable?"** If the schema is unstable or undocumented, default to narrow
per-leaf ignores plus a comment explaining why the parent folder is
deliberately *not* ignored.

## 4. Narrow Leaf-Ignore Over Folder-Ignore (Unknown-Schema Defense)

When ignoring **ephemeral state** inside a folder whose **future schema is
unknown** (third-party tool spool dirs, IDE per-session storage, generated
caches with versioned layouts), the agent **MUST NOT** ignore the parent
folder. Instead, ignore only the *known-ephemeral leaves*.

### Rationale

A trailing-slash folder ignore (`some/dir/`) hides every current AND future
file the tool emits in that folder. If the tool later adds a sibling artifact
the user would want to version-control, it is silently swallowed and never
surfaces in `git status`. Narrow leaf-ignores keep `git status` honest:
unknown siblings appear as untracked and force a deliberate triage decision.

### Rule

For any per-session / per-instance state folder whose contents are not a
closed, documented schema:

- Ignore each **leaf file** (`folder/*/state.json`) or **known-ephemeral
  subdirectory** (`folder/*/contents/`) explicitly.
- Do **NOT** ignore the enclosing per-session folder
  (`folder/*/`) — keep it un-ignored so future sibling files surface.
- Add an inline comment above the block explaining why the parent is
  deliberately not ignored.

### Companion `.gitattributes` Cleanup

When a `.gitattributes` filter / diff / textconv line targets a path that
now becomes gitignored, that line is dead config. Remove it in the same
commit (or an adjacent atomic commit) that introduces the narrowed ignore
rule.

### Canonical Example: VS Code Copilot Chat `chatEditingSessions/`

```gitignore
# Copilot Chat per-session undo/redo timeline (state.json) + content-addressed
# snapshots (contents/) — machine- and session-local; the canonical history of
# any edited file already lives in this repo's commit history, so these are pure
# redundant churn. Folder itself is NOT ignored so future, unknown sibling files
# surface for review.
…/workspaceStorage/*/chatEditingSessions/*/state.json
…/workspaceStorage/*/chatEditingSessions/*/contents/
```

### Anti-Pattern

```gitignore
# WRONG — hides every future artifact VS Code may add per session.
…/workspaceStorage/*/chatEditingSessions/
```

### Audit Cue

When a user asks to "ignore this whole tool state folder", first enumerate
the folder's current leaf set, classify each leaf as **ephemeral** or
**potentially-canonical**, and only ignore the ephemeral set with a comment
documenting the classification.
